title: Five rural homes listed near foraging locations across UK
summary:
Five residential properties located near foraging locations in England, Scotland and Wales have been listed for sale, with prices ranging from £775,000 to £1.25 million. The listings include properties in Brecon, Wiltshire, Somerset, Carmarthenshire and East Lothian.

title: £206k bridging loan funds Liverpool property renovation
summary:
A £206,000 bridging finance facility has been arranged to support the purchase and refurbishment of a six-bedroom detached property in Liverpool that had been vacant for over a decade. The 12-month facility enables the borrowers to complete renovation works before refinancing onto longer-term debt.

title: Housing security outweighs pension savings for UK retirees
summary:
Nearly half of UK adults prioritise outright homeownership over pension savings when planning for retirement, according to new research. A survey of 2,000 adults found that 45% cite outright home ownership as the most important factor for retirement security, compared with 36% who prioritise a large pension pot.

title: Estate agents warned over AI smart glasses privacy risks
summary:
Estate agents are being advised to update their compliance policies to address privacy concerns arising from AI-enabled smart glasses during property viewings. The guidance comes as consumers increasingly use devices such as Meta Glasses, which can capture photographs and video while connecting to AI-powered services.

The post Estate agents warned over AI smart glasses privacy risks appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Mansion tax threshold cut could widen property tax net
summary:
The proposed Mansion Tax could affect significantly more properties if the government reduces the threshold from £2 million to £1.5 million, with tax experts warning that fiscal drag could gradually expand its reach over time.

title: Industry calls for unified first-time buyer strategy
summary:
A mortgage broker has called on the Labour government to consolidate its first-time buyer support schemes into a cohesive strategy ahead of next week's party conference. Sarah Thompson of Mortgage Scout said that while progress had been made on individual measures, the schemes were not yet functioning as an integrated system.

title: Renters’ Rights Act shifts London lettings timing
summary:
The introduction of the Renters' Rights Act in May 2026 altered the typical seasonal pattern of London's lettings market, with peak summer activity arriving earlier than in previous years. Foxtons' latest index shows landlords secured tenancies earlier in the summer season following the rental reforms.

The post Renters’ Rights Act shifts London lettings timing appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: London property owners underpay £3.1bn in tax, report finds
summary:
London property owners are underpaying £3.1 billion in property taxes relative to home values, whilst households across the rest of England overpay, according to new research from the Resolution Foundation. The think tank's report highlights that residential property taxes have become disconnected from current house prices, creating significant regional disparities.

The post London property owners underpay £3.1bn in tax, report finds appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Triple Point provides £17m facility for Fulham development
summary:
Triple Point has originated a £17m development finance facility for a mixed-use residential scheme in Fulham, marking the largest single loan the lender's property development team has originated. The facility will fund construction of 31 apartments across two blocks alongside two commercial units off the King's Road.

The post Triple Point provides £17m facility for Fulham development appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Investor secures £335k bridge to settle enforcement order
summary:
A London-based property investor has secured a £335,000 bridging loan against an unencumbered buy-to-let property in Dollis Hill to meet a court-ordered liability arising from a planning enforcement dispute. The 24-month facility was provided by TAB against a property valued at £1 million, representing a loan-to-value ratio of 33.5%.
